eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office forecasts for London on May 20 position the daily maximum temperature near 20 °C, driven by a weak southerly airflow under broken cloud and modest insolation that limits further warming. Ensemble model runs from the UK Met Office and ECMWF show tight clustering around this value, consistent with late-May climatological norms for the region and current surface pressure patterns. Traders have therefore assigned near-certain implied probability to the 20 °C outcome, reflecting the narrow forecast range and limited upside risk from unexpected clear-sky development. A sudden increase in cloud cover or a shift in wind direction could still cap temperatures below this level before official verification at London City Airport.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance positions the highest temperature in London near 23 °C tomorrow under a weak Atlantic ridge that has replaced the southerly flow responsible for the 26.6 °C record at Kew Gardens on 19 May. This synoptic setup brings increased cloud cover and reduced insolation, limiting daytime radiative heating and aligning with late-May climatological norms. European and UK ensemble models show tight clustering around 22–24 °C, with only modest upside risk if breaks in cloud allow stronger surface warming. Traders have therefore concentrated implied probability on the 22–24 °C bands, reflecting the short-range forecast consensus ahead of official verification at London City Airport.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance and ensemble model runs position the highest temperature in London on May 22 near 27 °C, with a secondary cluster around 26–28 °C, under a weak Atlantic ridge that has replaced the southerly flow behind the 26.6 °C reading at Kew Gardens on 19 May. This setup brings increased cloud cover and reduced insolation, limiting daytime radiative heating and aligning with late-May climatological norms. European and UK ensemble models show tight clustering around 26–28 °C, with modest upside risk only if breaks in cloud allow stronger surface warming. Traders have therefore concentrated implied probability on the 26–28 °C bands, reflecting the short-range forecast consensus ahead of official verification at London City Airport.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from PAGASA and global models point to Manila highs in the mid-30s Celsius on May 22, supported by a persistent high-pressure ridge over the South China Sea that favors clear skies, intense solar heating, and light winds during afternoon peak hours. This setup aligns with May's climatological peak, when average daily maxima reach 33–35 °C, yet modest model spreads around 34–37 °C reflect uncertainty from potential shifts in steering flow or localized moisture convergence. Traders assign the highest implied probability to 36 °C because even slight reductions in cloud cover or humidity could push afternoon readings one to two degrees above the baseline forecast, while any increase in convective activity would favor the 35 °C outcome.
